policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Version 1.1 (December 2019) revises the June 2018 initial edition's Data Section to reflect the 2018 amendment to the Unfair Competition Prevention Act introducing protection for 'shared data with limited access' (effective July 1, 2019), while retaining the June 2018 AI Section. The guidelines are explicitly non-binding reference materials and model contracts intended to reduce transaction costs and foster B2B contracting practices without restricting freedom of contract. The Data Section addresses three contract types (data provision, data creation, and data sharing/platform), and the AI Section proposes an 'exploratory staged' development approach (assessment, PoC, development, and retraining) centered on quasi-mandate contracts and tailored usage conditions rather than strict IP ownership disputes. Although the guidelines impose no legal obligations or sanctions of their own, they highlight compliance considerations under existing Japanese laws (Personal Information Protection Act, Antimonopoly Act, Subcontract Act, Unfair Competition Prevention Act, Copyright Act, Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act) and international regimes such as the EU GDPR.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The METI Contract Guidelines on Utilization of AI and Data (v1.1) are predominantly framed around innovation enablement: both the Data and AI sections explicitly state their core purpose is to reduce transaction costs, establish practical contract models and exploratory development practices, preserve freedom of contract, and unlock open innovation and broader AI/data utilization. Economic competitiveness is a strong secondary frame, as the guidelines repeatedly justify lowering contractual friction by citing national and industrial competitiveness and surviving the Fourth Industrial Revolution; however, innovation enablement edges it out because the operative rationale centers on frictionless, voluntary ecosystem facilitation rather than zero-sum international rivalry. Fundamental rights appear as a tertiary consideration focused on preventing privacy infringements and complying with personal data protection laws (APPI and GDPR) during data sharing, while consumer/public safety (industrial plant safety, medical data, consumer contract protections) and national security (Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act export controls) appear only incidentally as sector examples or legal compliance checkpoints.

多様な立場に配慮したデータ契約の考え方や契約条項例等を用意するこ
とにより、データ利用の促進を図り、オープンイノベーションを促進するこ
とも、本ガイドライン（データ編）の一つの目的である。

evidence_spans.quote_en: By providing concepts for data contracts and model contract clauses that take diverse positions into account, promoting data utilization and fostering open innovation is also one of the purposes of these Guidelines (Data Section).

evidence_spans.source_section: AI編 第１ 総論 １ 目的
evidence_spans.quote_en: Thereby, by providing information for concluding rational contracts that both parties can agree to and helping to form contract practices, it aims to promote the development and utilization of software utilizing AI technology.

evidence_spans.quote_en: If parties can build low-cost and rational transactional relationships regarding data distribution and utilization, combined with the application of laws such as the Antimonopoly Act and the Unfair Competition Prevention Act, it is expected to enhance the competitiveness not only of the contracting parties but ultimately of the nation as a whole.
